newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds flat in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds flat in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Light buying failed to move U.S. mortage-backeds substantially above Tuesday's levels during a relatively quiet, abbreviated trading session Wednesday, market sources said.
Although many market players fled early for the Thanksgiving holiday, a few traders lingered to pick at a variety of mortgage products.
"We bought some Fannie Mae 15-years, we bought some discounts and we bought some 30-year Ginnie Maes," said one trader at a New York-based firm.
He said his outlook for the market remains bullish. "I like the market. I think it could do better."
But the nibbles were not significant enough to spark a rally in pass-throughs.
"I think the market is starting to analyze its bullish argument," said one Midwest-based trader.
He said he sees a few firms lightening up in the long end of the market, which may translate into downward pressure on prices.
By early afternoon Wednesday, pass-throughs were flat to 2/32 higher.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 7.0 percent coupons were up 2/32 at 99-05/32, yielding 104 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were 2/32 higher as well, at 100-29/32 and 99-05/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 2/32 at 102-23/32 to yield 6.13 percent.
PSA-The Bond market Trade Association has recommended 1400 EST/1900 GMT closings for the U.S. debt markets Wednesday and Friday, November 29, the organization said.
